classification.difficultyReason: Discover an unsignposted partition of all subsets into pairs differing by one fixed element, establish that it exhausts the subsets, and apply pigeonhole to force a nested selected pair.

content.prompt: Suppose a set contains precisely $n$ elements, where $n$ is a positive integer. Show that if more than half of the subsets of this set are selected, then there exist two selected subsets with the property that one is a subset of the other.

answer.short:
Fix $x\in S$ and pair each subset $A$ not containing $x$ with $A\cup\{x\}$.

There are $2^{n-1}$ pairs. Selecting more than $2^{n-1}$ subsets forces both members of one pair to be selected, and $A\subsetneq A\cup\{x\}$.
answer.worked:
Let $S$ be the given set and fix $x\in S$. Pair each subset $A\subseteq S\setminus\{x\}$ with $A\cup\{x\}$. Every subset of $S$ belongs to exactly one such pair.

There are $2^{n-1}$ pairs and $2^n$ subsets. More than half of the subsets means more than $2^{n-1}$ selected subsets. By the pigeonhole principle, some pair contains two selected subsets.

These subsets are $A$ and $A\cup\{x\}$, with $A\subsetneq A\cup\{x\}$. Therefore one selected subset is a subset of the other.
